quote: I ask no favors for my sex. I surrender not our claim to equality. All I ask of our brethren is, that they will take their feet from off our necks, and permit us to stand upright on that ground which God designed us to occupy.
source: Sarah Moore Grimké, Letters on the Equality of the Sexes, Letter II, to Mary S. Parker, 7th mo. 17, 1837 (Isaac Knapp, 1838)
note: Corrected: verified in the 1838 Isaac Knapp text, where the printed sentence opens with the word But. The quotation begins at I, so that one conjunction is dropped and nothing else is altered. The letter is dated Newburyport, 7th mo. 17, 1837, and addressed to Mary S. Parker.
